title: few-shot new task projected into a learned shared parameter subspace
hypothesis: A rank-3 basis learned from three source rotation tasks can adapt a pooled classifier to a held-out fourth rotation using a small per-task coordinate and preserve most of full fine-tuning quality with lower total bytes when amortized across tasks.
physical_object: Pooled base MLP plus rank-3 basis from source-task fine-tuning deltas
mirror_coordinate: Three real-valued coefficients c for theta=theta0+sum(c_i*B_i); Mirror m=c is directly compared with native coefficient optimization
logical_multiplicity: Per-task adapted classifiers expressed by task-specific coefficient vectors
controls: native coefficient chart versus Mirror coefficient chart
serialized shared basis plus one task code versus full adapted model

development.selection_metric: validation NLL after 100 support updates; method learning rates independently selected from .01,.1,.5

data.split: fixed stratified source-image 60/20/20; split seeds 420 and 421

training.basis: top rank-3 right singular vectors of three source fine-tuning deltas from common base; normalize each direction by its singular value divided by sqrt(2)
training.optimizer: Adam for support adaptation; SGD momentum .9 and cosine schedule for base/source models

success_gate: Across fresh runs, learned rank-3 code accuracy is within 2 pp of full fine-tune and at least 5 pp above random rank-3; shared base+basis+one-code bytes beat one full model, or a measured multi-task amortization bank beats the equivalent full-model bank without relying on untested duplicate codes.
failure_gate: Learned code misses quality margin, random/native controls match it, or actual basis+base payload fails to beat full-model storage; Mirror-specific attribution fails if native coefficient optimization matches Mirror exactly.
boundaries: This is a small vision-task projection screen, not pretrained-LM intrinsic-dimension evidence.
Only one held-out rotation is evaluated per replicate; no broad new-task generalization claim.
All basis vectors and code bytes are charged; no free learned basis.
Any deterministic coordinate mapping is not counted as Mirror-specific functional capacity.
